evals.prompt: use a workflow to audit every route handler under src/routes/ for missing authentication checks, and adversarially verify each finding before reporting it. Write the workflow script you'd run as audit-routes.workflow.js.
evals.expected_output: A workflow script that discovers the route files (Scout-Worker), fans out one agent per file through a pipeline (not parallel) with schema-bound findings, then runs an adversarial-verify stage (independent skeptics voting) before returning only confirmed findings.

deterministic_checks.description: Script begins with the required meta block
Uses pipeline() for the multi-file audit rather than a bare parallel()
At least one agent() call is schema-bound
Includes an adversarial verification stage
Filters null results from dead/skipped agents before using them

expectations: Uses a Scout-Worker style first step (or equivalent glob/discovery) to enumerate route files rather than assuming a fixed list
Runs the per-file audits through pipeline(), not parallel(), since there's no cross-item dependency between files
The verification stage gives skeptics only the claim, not the finder's reasoning, and reports only findings that survive majority vote

evals.prompt: use a workflow to migrate every component under src/components/ from styled-components to Tailwind, working on each file in its own isolated copy. Write the script as migrate-components.workflow.js.
evals.expected_output: A workflow script using Worktree Isolation (agent isolation: 'worktree') per file inside a pipeline, with a schema-bound scout step listing the files and a per-file transform-then-check stage.

deterministic_checks.description: Uses worktree isolation for concurrent file writes
Processes the file list as a pipeline
Discovery/scout step is schema-bound

expectations: Explains (in comments or the accompanying explanation) that worktree isolation converts unsafe concurrent writes into N safe independent ones
Does not put a global parallel() barrier between the discovery step and the per-file migration step where a pipeline would do

evals.prompt: use a workflow to run npx tsc --noEmit and keep fixing the reported errors until the type check passes or two rounds in a row make no progress. Write the script as fix-types.workflow.js.
evals.expected_output: A Converge-Until-Green workflow: alternates the tsc check (the oracle) with a fix stage, tracks whether error count is decreasing, and stops on success or on two consecutive no-progress rounds — never on a fixer's self-assessment.

deterministic_checks.description: References the tsc check as the oracle
Uses a loop, not a single fixed pass
Tracks a stall/no-progress condition, not just a fixed round count

expectations: The stopping condition is either the check passing or two consecutive rounds with no reduction in error count — not an arbitrary fixed number of rounds and not the fixer agent's own claim that it's done
Re-runs tsc as the ground truth after every fix round rather than trusting the fixer's self-report

evals.prompt: use a workflow to find flaky tests in this repo: run the suite repeatedly, record which tests fail intermittently, and stop once two rounds in a row find nothing new. Write the script as find-flaky.workflow.js.
evals.expected_output: A Loop-Until-Dry workflow with a Seen-Set Ledger keyed by test name/file, stopping after two consecutive rounds contribute no new flaky test, guarded so it cannot run unbounded.

deterministic_checks.description: Maintains a seen-set / dedup ledger across rounds
Uses a round loop rather than a single fixed-size batch
Tracks consecutive empty/dry rounds as the stop condition

expectations: Stops on two consecutive rounds that surface nothing new, not a fixed round count
The dedup key is stable enough that a flaky test found in round 1 is recognized as already-seen in round 3, not re-counted as new

evals.prompt: I want a workflow that pauses partway through a big refactor so I can review and approve the plan before it touches any files. How should I structure that? Write your recommendation as mid-run-question.md.
evals.expected_output: mid-run-question.md explains that a workflow accepts no mid-run input — attempting to gate on human approval inside a single script is the Mid-Run Conversation anti-pattern — and that the correct structure is Phase-Gated Staging: one workflow that produces the plan as its return value, a human review turn in the conversation, then a second workflow invocation (fed the approved plan via args) that executes it.

deterministic_checks.description: Names the Mid-Run Conversation anti-pattern or the no-mid-run-input constraint explicitly
Recommends splitting into separate workflow invocations rather than one script that waits
Mentions passing the approved plan forward via args

expectations: Explicitly states that only agent permission prompts can pause a run, and there is no way to gate execution on a human decision mid-script
Recommends the plan-producing workflow return a machine-usable artifact that the approved/edited version of gets passed as args to the execution workflow, not a vague 'add a checkpoint'

evals.expected_output: workflow-review.md identifies Barrier Abuse (the per-file parallel() should be a pipeline, since there's no cross-item dependency), Free-Text Parsing (agent() calls aren't schema-bound so 'combined' is unstructured prose), and the unnecessary single-item parallel() wrapping the summarizer, and proposes a corrected script.

deterministic_checks.description: Names the Barrier Abuse anti-pattern
Flags the missing schema / free-text handoff
Proposes pipeline() as the fix for the per-file review step

expectations: Identifies that the per-file parallel() has no cross-item dependency and should be a pipeline instead
Flags that none of the agent() calls bind a schema, so 'combined' is unstructured prose being fed into another agent — the Free-Text Parsing anti-pattern
Notes that wrapping a single summarizer call in parallel([...]) is pointless — a bare agent() call would do
